summary.tagline: A historic semi-natural tidal pool on the edge of the Atlantic Ocean.

travel.headline: Open Access Tidal Swimming
travel.reservation: There is no cost, no booking, nor any other imposed restriction to access the pool. It is maintained for the benefit of the community and visitors as a free amenity; however, users should check local conditions as it is a semi-natural tidal pool.

days.title: Atlantic Coast Swimming

stops.name: Bude Sea Pool
stops.detail: Swim in a safe haven for wild swimming located on the edge of the Atlantic Ocean at Summerleaze Beach.

days.driving: Allow for local walking times within Bude; conditions vary by tide
days.note: A suggested pace allows for multiple swim sessions depending on the tidal cycle.

intel.title: Universal Entry
intel.text: The pool is open for everyone to enjoy for free without prior booking. Access is dependent on tidal conditions at Summerleaze Beach.

intel.title: Tidal Influence
intel.text: As a semi-natural pool, water levels and safety are dictated by the Atlantic tides. Check local tide tables before arrival to ensure the pool is accessible.

intel.title: Local Bude Parking
intel.text: Evidence does not specify dedicated pool parking; visitors should verify local council parking availability in Bude. Summerleaze Beach typically serves as the primary access point.

intel.title: Town Amenities
intel.text: Fuel and supplies should be secured in the town of Bude. Availability of services directly at the pool site is not documented in official sources.

intel.title: Connectivity Status
intel.text: Mobile signal strength at the water's edge is unconfirmed. Visitors should not rely on digital maps for real-time safety updates while at the pool.

plan.arrival: Upon arrival in Bude, head toward Summerleaze Beach for local check-in at your accommodation and then walk to the pool area.
plan.vehicle: Local roads are suitable for standard cars; check for height restrictions in coastal car parks if using an RV.
plan.goldenHour: Summerleaze Beach coastal views, with seasonal caveats for Atlantic weather.
